## Diagnosis

The `default/app` Deployment was stuck mid-rollout. Diffing the two ReplicaSets showed the new revision differed from the healthy one by exactly one thing:

```
podAntiAffinity:
  requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
  - labelSelector: {matchLabels: {app: app}}
    topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
```

The cluster has **one** schedulable node (`...-control-plane`, no taints, 110 pod capacity, only 950m CPU / 290Mi memory requested). A *required* anti-affinity on `kubernetes.io/hostname` therefore permits at most **one** pod of the new template, so the scheduler correctly reported:

```
0/1 nodes are available: 1 node(s) didn't match pod anti-affinity rules.
```

The old ReplicaSet's 3 pods stayed Ready, masking the failure as "3/3" while `status` showed `updatedReplicas: 1` and a permanently `Pending` pod — and any replacement of an old pod could never have been scheduled.

## Fix

Patched the owning Deployment's pod template (the persistent resource that owns the faulty state), keeping the anti-affinity intent and all other settings untouched — the hard constraint became a soft preference:
